newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
* French socialists and their Communist allies scored a solid victory in the second round of parliamentary elections.
* A growing rift among negotiators in the tobacco talks have some vowing to propose a settlement that wouldn't necessarily include everyone involved in the deal.
* A letter from a lawyer for Digital Equipment Corp implies the company may be prepared to file an antitrust suit against Intel Corp in their patent dispute.
* The telephone service of movie listings, Moviefone, may offer a wealth of information to producers.
* Synthelabo, a unit of L'Oreal, has acquired the European rights to a new prostate cancer treatment from Praecis Pharmaceuticals for as much as $68 million.
* DreamWorks SKG has had only one of its shows chosen for the upcoming primetime TV season.
* Just months after it won a lawsuit allowing it to sell pagers that display up-to-the-second NBA scores, Motorola Inc has stopped promoting the device.
* Street.com, which operates an online financial news service, is pushing an advertising campaign that focuses on Chairman James Cramer.
* PointCast Inc, which pioneered "push" technology on the Internet, plans to release a new version of its software.
* The Edison Project, a venture into for-profit schools, plans to double its size over the next year.
* Cathleen Black, the president of Hearts Corp's magazine division, is shaking things up at the publishing company.
* A possible merger between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Inc a myriad of regulatory hurdles.

* The proposed merger between HFS Inc and CUC International Inc brings together two companies that specialise in products that have essentially have no cost to produce and offer primarily intangible benefits.
* Rockwell International Corp has shed some predictable, steady businesses and is relying more heavily on the volatile business of electronics.
